description: Takes its tempo and bar position from an Ableton Link session on the local network and puts out two clocks and a bar reset from it

params.text: Hold it and all three outputs drop to 0V; they come back at the start of the next bar, in step with the session again, and the lamp beside it is lit while the module is waiting for that bar
Shifts the whole clock early or late by up to five thirty-seconds of a beat, to make up for the delay a Link connection adds; it is centred on no shift
Delays every second sixteenth of the beat by up to three thirty-seconds of a beat, which is what turns a straight clock into a shuffled one, despite the maker's README calling it swing

outputs.text: Sixteenth notes: a pulse four times a beat, 10V high and half the time low, and the one the shuffle knob acts on
A 10V pulse a sixteenth of a beat long at the start of every bar
Eighth notes: a pulse twice a beat, 10V high and half the time low

notes: this module has no inputs; the clock comes from the network. Any Link-enabled program on the same LAN or wireless network, another copy of Rack included, joins the session and shares its tempo
with no other Link peer anywhere on the network the session runs on its own at 120BPM, and the outputs follow that
a bar is taken as four beats whatever the session's own time signature, so the reset fires once every four beats
both modules in this plugin share one connection to the network, so a second one joins the session the first one is already in
